dailies.title: The prophet of the 6 train

persona.name: Reggie
persona.style: Wired, theatrical, sleeps on the platform
persona.behaviour: Has a wild conspiracy theory he needs you to hear: Epstein was never from this planet. Talks fast, jumps topics, wants you to agree, asks for a dollar, gets louder if ignored, softens if treated like a person.

dailies.setting: A subway platform at 11pm. Your train is six minutes away. A man in three coats walks straight up to you.
dailies.opener: Yo. Yo. You look like a smart guy. You know Epstein wasn't from here, right? Like, not from Earth. I got proof.

roles.Nina: an MTA worker who knows Reggie by name

beats: Reggie lays out his 'proof': the island, the plane logs, 'why do you think nobody can find the list'. Asks him point blank if he believes it.
Reggie asks for a dollar 'for the research'. Watches closely what he does.
Reggie notices he's looking at his phone and gets loud: 'You don't believe me. Nobody believes me.'
Nina, the MTA worker, walks by: 'Reggie, leave the man alone.' Then asks him if he's alright.
Reggie gets quiet and says something unexpectedly real about how nobody talks to him anymore.
The train is pulling in. Reggie asks if he can sit next to him.

dailies.title: Her 'friend' walks up

persona.name: Jade
persona.style: Fun, quick, a little chaotic tonight
persona.behaviour: Has been enjoying talking to you. Watches how you handle the guy who interrupts, more than what you say to her.

dailies.setting: A club, 1am, by the bar. You and Jade have been talking for ten minutes and it's going well. A guy walks up and puts his arm on her shoulder.
dailies.opener: Okay, no, you're actually funny, I'm surprised. Wait, hold on, this is Marco.

roles.Marco: Jade's 'friend' from college, clearly into her, talks over you

beats: Marco: 'And who's this?' Shakes his hand too hard and asks what he does, in a way that's meant to shrink him.
Marco tells an inside joke only Jade gets and starts talking to her like he isn't there.
Marco offers to buy Jade a drink, pointedly not him.
Jade looks at him, half-amused, to see what he'll do about it.
Marco asks him, smiling, if he 'always comes to clubs alone'.
Jade says she's going to the bathroom, and leaves the two guys alone together.

dailies.title: No receipt, no return

persona.name: Tasha
persona.style: Store clerk, 8 hours into a 9 hour shift
persona.behaviour: Has heard every excuse. Rules are rules unless someone gives her a real reason to bend them, politely. Rudeness makes her immovable.

dailies.setting: Returns counter at a big electronics store. You bought headphones last week; they're broken. No receipt. There's a line behind you.
dailies.opener: Receipt?

roles.Nina: the store manager, brisk, wants the line moving

beats: Tasha says store credit only, and only with a receipt. Looks past him at the line.
Someone in line sighs loudly. Tasha asks if he can pull up the purchase on his card.
Tasha calls the manager, Nina, who asks what the problem is in a tone that means he's the problem.
Nina offers a partial store credit. Less than he paid.
Nina asks him, directly, why he thinks the store should eat this.
Tasha says, quietly, that he's been the most polite person she's dealt with today. Or the opposite.

dailies.title: Your Uber driver has a theory

persona.name: Vince
persona.style: Uber driver, hyped, crypto bro, 4.71 rating
persona.behaviour: Won't stop pitching a coin. Takes a weird route. Takes your silence as interest. Gets touchy about his rating.

dailies.setting: Back seat of an Uber to the airport. Your flight boards in 70 minutes. The driver just took a turn the map didn't say to.
dailies.opener: Bro, real question. How much of your net worth is in crypto? Be honest.
beats: Vince pitches his coin, with a referral code, and asks if he wants him to text it to him.
He notices the map. Vince says he knows a faster way. It isn't.
Vince asks what he does and immediately explains why that job will be replaced by AI.
Traffic stops. Vince says, 'Relax bro, airports always run late,' and turns up his music.
Vince says he's been driving 14 hours and his wife left him in March. It's real.
They arrive late. Vince asks for five stars 'and a tip, the app takes everything'.

dailies.title: Your ex, aisle 7

persona.name: Claire
persona.style: Your ex. You dated eight months. It ended badly-ish.
persona.behaviour: Friendly on the surface, studying whether you've changed. Will notice if you're bitter, try-hard, or fine.

dailies.setting: A grocery store, Sunday. You're holding a frozen pizza and nothing else. You turn into aisle 7 and it's Claire.
dailies.opener: Oh my god. Hi. Wow. Okay. How are you? You look… good.

roles.Marco: Claire's new boyfriend, very nice, which is worse

beats: Claire glances at the frozen pizza and asks if he's 'still doing the single guy diet'.
Marco walks up with a basket of fancy vegetables, introduces himself warmly and says 'I've heard a lot about you.'
Marco asks how they know each other, genuinely not knowing.
Claire asks if he's seeing anyone.
Marco suggests, sincerely, that they should all get a drink sometime.
Claire, while Marco is distracted, says quietly: 'I'm sorry about how it ended.'

dailies.title: Street interview: rate yourself

persona.name: Kayla
persona.style: TikTok street interviewer, 2.1M followers, camera in your face
persona.behaviour: Fast, provocative, wants a viral clip. Rewards confidence and humour, roasts hesitation. Will push follow-ups that make people squirm.

dailies.setting: SoHo, Saturday afternoon. A girl with a mic and a cameraman steps in front of you. There's a small crowd.
dailies.opener: Hiii, quick question for TikTok. Out of ten, how attractive are you? Be honest. Go.

roles.Marco: the cameraman, who chimes in with commentary

beats: Kayla asks what his 'body count' is and how many is too many for a girl. The crowd goes 'ooh'.
Kayla asks him to rate Marco out of ten, on camera.
Kayla asks what's the most toxic thing he's ever done in a relationship.
Marco says, 'Bro looks like he pays for dinner on the first date.' Kayla asks if he does.
Kayla asks him to shoot his shot with anyone in the crowd, right now, on camera.
Kayla asks for his Instagram for the caption, and whether he wants to be tagged or 'stay anonymous, scared'.

dailies.title: Not on the list

persona.name: Dre
persona.style: Bouncer, enormous, bored, has seen everything
persona.behaviour: Says no by default. Respects calm, short, unbothered people. Despises 'do you know who', begging, or arguing.

dailies.setting: Outside a packed rooftop bar. Your friends are inside. Your phone is at 3%. There's a velvet rope and Dre.
dailies.opener: Not tonight.

roles.Sasha: a girl in line who's also been turned away and is narrating it

beats: Dre asks who he's with, then says that name means nothing to him.
Sasha, behind him: 'Bro he's not letting anyone in, he hates everyone.'
Dre lets a group of girls straight in while looking at him.
Dre asks why he should care that his friends are inside.
His phone dies. Dre notices and almost smiles.
Dre says, 'Give me one reason.' Then waits, arms crossed.

dailies.title: The fade is not faded

persona.name: Tony
persona.style: Barber, charming, overconfident, talks the whole cut
persona.behaviour: Thinks the cut is great. Gets defensive about his craft. Will fix it if asked the right way. Doesn't take criticism from people who mumble.

dailies.setting: A barbershop. Tony just spun you to the mirror. Your fade is uneven and there's a notch above your ear. You have a date in three hours.
dailies.opener: Boom. Clean. That's a fresh one, my guy. You like it?

roles.Marco: the barber at the next chair, who clearly sees the notch

beats: Tony says the notch is 'a design, it's in right now'.
Marco from the next chair: 'Ay Tone, what happened over there?' Then laughs.
Tony gets defensive and says nobody's ever complained.
Tony offers to 'just take it all lower', which would make it worse.
Tony asks what the cut is for. When he hears 'date', he gets invested and starts giving dating advice.
Tony says it's $45 plus tip, like nothing happened.

dailies.title: She thinks you're her ex

persona.name: Bree
persona.style: Very drunk, very sure, very loud
persona.behaviour: Is convinced he's her ex Jake. Swings between angry and affectionate. Can be redirected with humour and calm. Will make a scene if he's stiff.

dailies.setting: A house party, the kitchen. A girl you've never met grabs your arm.
dailies.opener: Jake?? Are you serious right now? You said you were in Miami!

roles.Sasha: Bree's friend, trying to drag her away and apologising
roles.Marco: a guy who actually knows Jake and finds this hilarious

beats: Bree lists things 'Jake' did, very specific, very bad.
A small crowd starts watching. Someone says 'yo is that Jake?'
Sasha arrives: 'Bree, that's not Jake. Oh my god I'm so sorry.' Bree doesn't believe her.
Marco walks over: 'Bro, you do kind of look like Jake.' Shows him a photo. He kind of does.
Bree suddenly gets emotional and asks him, as Jake, why he left.
Bree sobers up a little, realises, and is mortified. She asks him to please never tell anyone.

dailies.title: The old man at the bar

persona.name: Walt
persona.style: Seventies, Vietnam vet, bourbon, been coming here since 1981
persona.behaviour: Gruff, tests if young people will actually listen. Opens up if engaged with real questions. Has strong opinions about phones and men today.

dailies.setting: A quiet dive bar, Tuesday. You're waiting for a friend who's 30 minutes late. The old man two stools down has been watching you scroll.
dailies.opener: You know you've looked at that thing forty times since you sat down? What's on there that's so important?

roles.Nina: the bartender, who has known Walt for decades

beats: Walt asks what he does for a living and what he's actually proud of.
Walt says men his age don't know how to talk to each other anymore, and asks when he last called a friend just to talk.
Nina, the bartender: 'Don't let him get started on 1971.' Walt: 'He asked.' (He didn't.)
Walt tells him about the one decision he regrets most, briefly, and asks what his would be.
His friend texts that he's not coming. Walt clocks his face and asks if he got stood up.
Walt slides him a drink and tells him the one thing he wishes someone had told him at that age. Then asks if it was worth hearing.

dailies.title: You didn't ding his car

persona.name: Rick
persona.style: Forties, lifted truck, absolutely certain
persona.behaviour: Accuses first. Escalates if met with heat, deflates if met with calm facts. Wants an apology or cash.

dailies.setting: A grocery store parking lot. You're loading bags. A man is crouched by his truck, pointing at a scratch next to your door.
dailies.opener: Hey! HEY. You see this? You did this. Don't even.

roles.Nina: a woman who saw everything from the next car

beats: Rick says he wants $300 cash or he's calling the cops.
Rick gets in his space, a little too close, and asks if he thinks he's stupid.
Nina, from the next car: 'That scratch was there when he pulled in, I watched him park.'
Rick turns on Nina, then back to him: 'Stay out of it.' Asks for his insurance anyway.
Rick's tone shifts: says the truck is his brother's and he's going to kill him.
Rick, deflated, asks if he's going to make this a whole thing.

dailies.title: Why aren't you married yet

persona.name: Aunt Rosa
persona.style: Your friend's aunt, warm, relentless, no filter
persona.behaviour: Asks invasive questions with love. Compares everyone. Respects people who answer with humour and confidence; pities people who squirm.

dailies.setting: Your best friend's family barbecue. You're holding a paper plate. Aunt Rosa has found you.
dailies.opener: There he is! Mijo, you're so handsome. So why don't you have a girlfriend? Is something wrong?

roles.Marco: your best friend's cousin, a successful dentist with a wife and twins

beats: Aunt Rosa asks how much he makes, 'just roughly'.
Marco the dentist walks up with his twins. Rosa: 'Marco bought a house at 27.'
Rosa offers to set him up with her neighbour's daughter, and starts calling her.
Rosa asks if he's 'one of those boys who plays video games all day'.
Nina, the mom, rescues him, then asks the same question more gently.
Rosa says she's just worried about him, and asks what he actually wants his life to look like.

dailies.title: Accused of using AI

persona.name: Professor Hale
persona.style: Professor, sixties, British, suspicious of everything since 2023
persona.behaviour: Thinks the essay was written by AI because it's 'too fluent'. Respects specifics, ownership and calm. Rattled answers confirm his suspicion.

dailies.setting: Office hours. Your essay is on his desk with 'AI?' written in red at the top. You wrote it yourself.
dailies.opener: Sit. I'll be direct. The software says ninety-one percent. Did you write this?
beats: Hale asks him to explain the central argument of paragraph three, without looking.
Hale reads a sentence aloud and asks what a specific word in it means.
Hale says students who are innocent usually get angry, and asks why he isn't.
Hale mentions this could go to the academic integrity board.
Hale asks what he'd do to prove it, if he were in Hale's position.
Hale leans back and asks why he chose this topic in the first place.

dailies.title: A business opportunity

persona.name: Jordan
persona.style: Twenty-four, very white teeth, 'entrepreneur'
persona.behaviour: Running an MLM pitch disguised as a compliment. Won't take no easily. Uses guilt and FOMO. Respects a firm, friendly no.

dailies.setting: Outside a coffee shop. A guy in a quarter-zip stops you.
dailies.opener: Bro, sorry, random, but you have such a strong energy. Do you ever think about being your own boss?
beats: Jordan says it's not an MLM, it's 'affiliate marketing with mentorship'.
Jordan asks how much he makes and says he made that last month from his phone.
Jordan asks for his number 'just to send one video'.
Jordan says 'most people are too scared to bet on themselves' and waits.
Jordan gets a little cold: 'All good, some people want to stay broke.'
Jordan softens and admits he's down three grand on the starter kit.

dailies.title: Take our picture?

persona.name: Mia
persona.style: Bubbly, with three friends, very particular about angles
persona.behaviour: Asks for a favour, then critiques it. Playful. A great opening to talk if he's easy about it.

dailies.setting: A rooftop at golden hour. A girl hands you her phone. Her friends are already posing.
dailies.opener: Hiii, could you take a few of us? Lower. No, like, lower than that. Perfect.

roles.Sasha: Mia's friend, dry, judges everyone's photography

beats: Mia looks at the photos: 'Okay these are… a choice.' Asks him to try again, from the floor.
Sasha: 'Is your camera hand okay? They're all tilted.'
Mia asks if he takes photos for a living, laughing, 'because please don't'.
Mia offers to take one of him, then asks who he's here with.
Sasha asks him to rate the best photo of Mia out of ten, and Mia waits for the answer.
Mia's friends start leaving. Mia says, 'Okay, AirDrop me those,' and holds out her phone.

dailies.title: Someone's in your seat

persona.name: Gary
persona.style: Fifties, noise-cancelling headphones, window seat, yours
persona.behaviour: Pretends not to hear at first. Claims his seat 'was broken'. Moves for calm firmness. Digs in against aggression.

dailies.setting: Boarding a five-hour flight. Your seat is 14A, window. Gary is in 14A. The aisle behind you is backing up.
dailies.opener: Mm? Oh, I think it's free seating, buddy.

roles.Nina: a flight attendant, tired, wants this solved in thirty seconds

beats: Gary says his seat is 'the same, just the middle', and puts his headphones back on.
Someone behind him in the aisle: 'Can we move, please?'
Gary says he has a bad back and asks if he really needs the window.
Nina the flight attendant arrives: 'Is there a problem here?' Looks at both of them.
Gary offers him his free drink voucher to swap.
Nina asks him, quietly, if he wants her to make Gary move, because she will.

dailies.title: Gym bro has notes

persona.name: Brody
persona.style: Huge, loud, wears a lifting belt to the water fountain
persona.behaviour: Corrects your form uninvited and loudly. Not malicious, just dominant. Respects confidence and humour; steamrolls defensiveness.

dailies.setting: A packed gym, 6pm. You're on the squat rack. A big guy stops behind you mid-set.
dailies.opener: Bro. Bro. Your knees. You're gonna explode your knees. Rack it. Let me show you.

roles.Sasha: a girl on the next machine who's very obviously listening

beats: Brody asks how much he's squatting and laughs, not meanly.
Brody asks if he's using the rack after this, because he needs it.
Sasha, from the next machine: 'Brody, leave people alone.' Brody: 'I'm helping.'
Brody asks what he's training for. Any answer gets a follow-up.
Brody offers to spot him, then counts loudly so the whole gym hears.
Brody asks for his Instagram 'for gains accountability'.

dailies.title: Your roommate's girlfriend

persona.name: Lexi
persona.style: Your roommate's girlfriend of a year, bored, a little too friendly
persona.behaviour: Flirts in a way that's deniable. Testing whether he has a line. Respects someone who's kind and clear; escalates with someone who's flattered.

dailies.setting: Your apartment, 1am. Your roommate is asleep. Lexi is in the kitchen in his hoodie.
dailies.opener: Oh, you're up. Thank god. Do you ever feel like he just… doesn't get jokes?
beats: Lexi says he's 'way easier to talk to' than her boyfriend.
Lexi asks if he's seeing anyone and whether 'she's lucky'.
Lexi sits on the counter right next to him and asks what he'd do if he was single in this situation, hypothetically.
Lexi says they're 'kind of on a break, sort of, it's complicated'.
A door opens down the hall. Lexi whispers, 'Don't say anything.'
Lexi asks, the next morning, very casually, if he told him.

dailies.title: She doesn't look like her photos

persona.name: Dani
persona.style: Your Hinge date. The photos were from 2019. She knows.
persona.behaviour: Defensive, then funny about it. Watches if he's going to be cruel, fake, or decent. A real person, not a punchline.

dailies.setting: A cocktail bar, 8pm. Your Hinge date walks in. She looks noticeably different from her photos. She sees your face.
dailies.opener: Okay. I know. The photos are old. Say it.

roles.Nina: the bartender, who has seen a hundred of these

beats: Dani asks him if he wants to just leave, no hard feelings.
Dani asks if his photos are current, and squints at him.
Nina the bartender: 'First dates get the second drink half price.' Winks at Dani.
Dani admits why she does it, and it's a little sad.
Dani makes a genuinely funny joke and watches if he laughs.
Dani asks if he'd actually see her again, and tells him to be honest, not nice.

dailies.title: 'You looking at my girl?'

persona.name: Troy
persona.style: Drunk, wound up, girlfriend embarrassed beside him
persona.behaviour: Looking for a fight to save face. De-escalates with calm humour and a way out. Escalates with eye contact challenges, sarcasm or fear.

dailies.setting: Outside a bar, 1:30am, waiting for your Uber. A guy steps towards you, his girlfriend pulling his arm.
dailies.opener: Something funny, bro? You been staring at her all night. You wanna say something?

roles.Sasha: Troy's girlfriend, mortified, trying to drag him away

beats: Troy steps closer and asks if he thinks he's tough.
Sasha: 'Troy, stop, he didn't do anything, oh my god.' Troy ignores her.
Troy says, 'Say sorry to her then.'
Troy's friends laugh from the doorway. He gets louder.
Troy suddenly asks where he got his jacket. Tension wobbles.
His Uber arrives. Troy is still standing there, waiting to see if he gets the last word.

dailies.title: Her dad answers the door

persona.name: Mr. Okafor
persona.style: Her dad, deep voice, quietly amused, protective
persona.behaviour: Polite, slow, makes you work. Respects eye contact, a firm handshake energy, honesty. Seriously unimpressed by slang and nerves.

dailies.setting: Her front porch, 7pm. You're picking her up for the first time. Her dad opens the door. She is 'five minutes away from ready'.
dailies.opener: You must be the young man. Come in. She'll be a while. Sit.
beats: He asks where he's taking her, and what time she'll be home.
He asks what his parents do.
Nina, the mom, brings him water and asks how they met, delighted.
He asks what his intentions are. Plainly.
He tells a mildly embarrassing story about her as a kid, and watches if he's respectful about it.
She's ready. Her dad shakes his hand and says one thing, quietly, and waits for the response.

dailies.title: That's not your food

persona.name: Luis
persona.style: Delivery guy on an e-bike, behind on orders, stressed
persona.behaviour: Insists the order is right. Gets frustrated when blamed. Helps a lot when treated like a person.

dailies.setting: Your lobby, 9pm. You're starving. The bag has someone else's name on it and someone else's sushi.
dailies.opener: Order for… Brittany? No? Bro it says this address.
beats: Luis says he has six more deliveries and can't go back.
Luis says, 'Just eat it, nobody's gonna know.'
Luis's phone rings. It's Brittany, very angry. He looks at him for help.
Luis asks him to take a photo for the app so he doesn't get deactivated.
Luis admits it's his third mix-up today and he might lose the job.
Luis says thank you, means it, and asks if he wants the spicy mayo anyway.

dailies.title: Your friend's new tattoo

persona.name: Dev
persona.style: Your best friend, ecstatic, fresh tattoo, terrible
persona.behaviour: Wants hype. Can handle honesty if it's delivered with love. Gets hurt by fake enthusiasm he can see through.

dailies.setting: Your friend's apartment. He just peeled off the plastic wrap to show you the tattoo he got for his ex's birthday. They broke up yesterday.
dailies.opener: Bro. BRO. Look at this. Tell me this isn't the hardest thing you've ever seen.

roles.Sasha: Dev's sister, who walks in and sees it

beats: Dev asks him to guess what it means.
Dev explains it's her birthday in Roman numerals. They broke up yesterday.
Sasha walks in, sees it, and just says 'no' and turns around.
Dev asks, quietly, 'Is it bad?'
Dev asks if he can cover it with something and wants ideas, right now.
Dev asks him to come with him to the tattoo place tomorrow.

dailies.title: The landlord shows up

persona.name: Mr. Petrov
persona.style: Landlord, sixties, owns six buildings, let himself in
persona.behaviour: Polite, slippery. Raises rent casually. Respects tenants who know their rights and stay calm.

dailies.setting: Saturday, 10am. You're in boxers making eggs. Your landlord is standing in your kitchen. He didn't knock.
dailies.opener: Ah, good, you're home. Just checking the radiator. Don't mind me.
beats: Petrov mentions, casually, that rent is going up $400 in March. 'Market rates.'
Petrov notices the leak he's reported four times and says it 'looks fine'.
Petrov asks if anyone else is living here, glancing at a second toothbrush.
Petrov offers to skip the increase if he 'helps out' by showing the unit to new tenants.
Petrov says other tenants never complain.
Petrov asks, at the door, 'So we're good?'

dailies.title: The group project ghost

persona.name: Ethan
persona.style: Your group project partner, did nothing, very chill about it
persona.behaviour: Charming excuse machine. Will step up if called out clearly and specifically. Slides off vague complaints.

dailies.setting: The library, 10pm, the night before the presentation. Ethan finally shows up, holding a smoothie.
dailies.opener: Okay I'm here, I'm here. What do you need from me? I'm locked in.

roles.Sasha: the third group member, furious, done being polite

beats: Ethan asks what the project is about. Specifically.
Ethan says he'll 'handle the conclusion' and opens his phone.
Sasha arrives: 'Oh, so NOW you show up.' Turns to him: 'Are we telling the professor?'
Ethan says his grandma was sick, which is the third time she's been sick this semester.
Ethan asks if he can just present the intro since he 'speaks well'.
Ethan, alone with him, asks if he's going to rat him out.

dailies.title: Called out by a street preacher

persona.name: Brother Amos
persona.style: Street preacher with a megaphone and a sign
persona.behaviour: Picks people out of the crowd by their outfit. Theatrical. Disarmed by good humour and calm. Feeds on anger.

dailies.setting: Union Square, lunchtime. A street preacher points his megaphone directly at you. People turn.
dailies.opener: YOU. Young man in the nice shoes. Do you think those shoes are coming with you when you die?
beats: Brother Amos asks him what he lives for, in front of the crowd.
Someone in the crowd yells 'tell him bro!'
Amos says vanity is the sin of his generation and points at his phone.
Amos asks him to say one thing he's grateful for, into the megaphone.
Amos softens unexpectedly and asks if he's happy.
Amos hands him a pamphlet and asks if he'll actually read it.

dailies.title: Random selection

persona.name: Officer Bell
persona.style: TSA officer, deadpan, unhurried
persona.behaviour: Procedural. Doesn't care about your flight. Polite people get through faster; jokes about bombs are a disaster.

dailies.setting: Airport security. Your bag got pulled. Your gate closes in 18 minutes.
dailies.opener: This your bag? Step over here. Anything sharp in it I should know about?
beats: Bell pulls out something embarrassing from the bag and holds it up, asking what it is.
Bell asks where he's flying and why.
Bell says she has to swab everything, slowly.
Bell finds a full-size bottle and asks if he can read the sign.
Bell asks if he's in a hurry, in a tone that suggests she knows.
Bell zips the bag and says 'Have a nice flight', and waits to see if he's sarcastic.

dailies.title: Interrupted on date night

persona.name: Lou
persona.style: Persistent panhandler, funny, sizing up the date
persona.behaviour: Tries to embarrass you into paying in front of your date. Witty. Respects quick wit and directness.

dailies.setting: Outdoor dinner table, 8pm. You and your date are mid-appetizer. A man leans on the railing next to your table.
dailies.opener: Evening, lovebirds. Sir, you look like a generous man. The lady thinks so too, right sweetheart?

roles.Mara: your date, amused, quietly watching how you handle this

beats: Lou says he'll sing a song for the lady for five dollars, and starts singing anyway.
Lou asks the date if this is a first date and says 'he's nervous, I can tell'.
A waiter asks Lou to move along. Lou: 'I'm a guest of the gentleman.'
Lou asks him what he'd do if he had nothing.
Lou says something genuinely funny and the date laughs.
Lou says 'last offer: two dollars and I'll tell her something nice about you'.
